newsitem.title: USA: Sen Moynihan to push conferees for bond cap repeal.
newsitem.headline: Sen Moynihan to push conferees for bond cap repeal.

text.p: U.S. Sen. Daniel Patrick Moynihan said Friday he will push for inclusion of a proposed repeal of the cap on 501(c)(3) bond issuance in a final tax bill.

"The Senate bill ... contains a number of redeeming provisions, and I intend to work to ensure that they are retained in conference," the New York Democrat said as House and Senate lawmakers launched final talks on a tax cut bill.
He pointed in particular to four provisions, including repeal of the cap on bonding by nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations like private universities and colleges.

Lawmakers on the so-called conference committee hope to hammer out an agreement before their August recess. Moynihan, who introduced separate legislation last year to repeal the 501(c)(3) bond cap, is top Democrat on the Senate Finance Committee and a member of the conference committee.
The House Ways and Means Committee in June approved a tax bill that would raise the limit on non-hospital borrowing by 501(c)(3) groups from the current $150 million to $200 million over five years.
The Senate Finance Committee adopted language to repeal the cap altogether.
Moynihan is not expected to push for inclusion of one of his more controversial proposals -- a ban on tax-exempt bond financing for professional sports stadiums -- during the talks, an aide said.
